title: SIU clears officer in Ajax man's fatal shooting
subtitle: Home invasion suspects tried to flee in truck
article: The fatal shooting of an Ajax man by police pursuing suspects in a home invasion earlier this year was justified, according to a report released by the province's Special Investigations Unit (SIU).

Shelton McKenzie, 21, died after York police fired upon a truck that sped toward officers investigating a home invasion robbery in Markham April 13. He died after being struck in the head by a shotgun blast.
Mr. McKenzie and another Ajax man, who was also shot by police, ignored repeated orders to surrender, SIU Deputy Director James Ramsay concluded.
Mr. Ramsay said in a statement "police acted commendably in very difficult circumstances."

York police responded to a 911 call about a home invasion on Steele Valley Road around 5:15 a.m. April 13, setting up a perimeter around the property. Two men had entered the home and loaded cash and property into the family's pickup truck.

Officers confronted the suspects as they backed out of the garage and Mr. McKenzie, the driver, accelerated when he saw cops, the SIU said. Several shots were fired by police when the driver and passenger ignored orders to get out of the vehicle and surrender. None of the seven shots hit either man in the truck.
As the truck began moving forward an officer in its path fired a blast from his shotgun, striking Mr. McKenzie in the head.
A passenger leapt from the truck and ran off. The man, who had been slightly wounded by police fire, was apprehended a short time later.
Kevin Harris, 26, of Ajax, was charged with armed robbery, forcible confinement and wearing a disguise.
The SIU is a civilian agency that investigates incidents in which civilians are seriously hurt or killed during interactions with police.
